name: gelliusBathDeath
source:
Based on all the representations of the Afterlife that Gellius had encountered during his lifetime, none had prepared him for the truth. The Afterlife was, for the lack of a better word, just your average bathroom. In the large cast iron bathtub sat Death. He lazily pushed a skeletal rubber ducky with a boney finger. *Vroomsh! * noises rolled out of his lipless mouth. 
 
 `` Is this hell?'' Gellius asked visibly uncomfortable. `` Because I ca n't imagine it being Heaven. Sorry.'' Gellius always made a point of being polite. 
 
 `` Oh, no,'' Death replied, dunking the rubber ducky under the water. It returned to the surface with a refreshing *plop*. `` I just needed a bath. I played chess with Pestilence. Last time I did that was in 1347 and I did n't take a bath afterwards. Well... Let's just say it meant working overtime. You'll know all that stuff soon enough, though.'' 
 
 `` What?'' 
 
 `` Yeah, did n't Peter tell you? You've been assigned to replace me. According to Anu and Muhammed, who are chairing the Committee for the Replacement of the Representation of Death, you were the ideal candidate.'' 
 
 Gellius chuckled. He was not surprised to hear this. Being dead certainly changed your perspective on things. He was, however, very much confused by all of this. 
 
 `` Anu? Muhammed? Committee? Is this the part where you reveal to me that all the myths, legends and faiths are true, *and* the Afterlife is run like a failing corporation?'' 
 
 Death pondered this for a moment while splashing the water - making waves for the ducky to ride. 
 
 `` No. Not *all* the myths are true. Jesus' body is not present in the bread, nor is his blood present in the wine. That's really dumb. Scientology only has it partly right.'Xenu' did not do all those things. Tom Cruise did.'' 
 
 `` *What. *'' 
 
 `` Yeah, y'know. The Eternal Return of Zeus, Christ, Cruise.'' Death let out something resembling a sigh as he stood up, using a blanket to cover his modesty had he had any. Still dripping, he carefully stepped out of the tub. 
 
 `` Look,'' he continued. `` The moment you take over, it will all make sense to you...'' 
 
 `` But I do n't *want* to be Death!'' Gellius interjected. Certainly he would have a say in the matter? 
 
 `` I guess, but you also did not want to die. And that happened. So, yeah...'' 
 
 `` That makes no sense!'' interjected Gellius again, this time more fiercely. 
 
 `` I guess. Or rather... Not yet, anyway. Look, you have been selected for the job, and it really is interesting. Omnipresence is not something you humans get to experience all that often. You'll go places. Meet people. The secondary benefits are *o-kay*. Unless they changed the contract, you can overturn Destiny and/or Chance thrice a century. Quite a blast. Also, you'll know *The Truth*, about *Everything*.'' 
 
 Gellius' mind raced as his eyes scanned the bathroom. The shower curtain had a pink'Hello Skully' pattern. Accepting the fact he had no say in the matter, Gellius turned his attention back to Death, who was drying his bones with a rose-coloured towel. 
 
 `` Well, alright. Just one question...'' 
 
 `` Shoot. We have all eternity.'' 
 
 ``... What? Err... Right. Omnipresence. Anyway, is the skeletal'Grim Reaper' thing mandatory?'' 
 
 Death shook his skull. 
 
 `` Nah. You'll be the representation of Death, but how you represent yourself is up to you. One of the perks. My predecessor did the perky, sexy goth girl thing. Her predecessor always took the form of the deceased's loved ones.'' 
 
 `` How did your predecessor be a goth girl if you've been working since the 14th century?'' 
 
 `` Omni-'' 
 
 ``... presence, right. Got it. I think.'' 
 
 By now Death had put on his robes. 
 
 `` Ready?'' He asked. 
 
 `` I guess?'' 
 
 Death simply nodded. Extending a bony finger, he touched Gellius' forehead. And that was that.
retelling:
Narrated by **Death**, the enigmatic being who has decided it's time for a change:

In the quiet and ordinary sanctuary of an average bathroom, bathed in a soft pink light from a 'Hello Skully' patterned shower curtain, I found myself in the midst of preparing to retire. A simple task, one that has been repeated countless times over the millennia, yet today held a unique twist - the selection of my successor.

As I submerged myself in the warm waters of the cast iron bathtub, I felt a familiar presence - Pestilence, my perpetual chess partner and confidant. We had played across the ages, our games marking significant events in history. But today was not for games; today, I was here to pass on the mantle of Death.

With a sense of foreboding, I called forth Peter, a messenger with whom I've shared many a secret. He delivered the news that would change the lives of both Gellius and myself - Gellius had been chosen as my successor. The decision had not been made lightly; it was the result of careful deliberations by members of the Committee for the Replacement of the Representation of Death, including Anu and Muhammed.

As I explained to Gellius the responsibilities that would accompany his new role, I felt a pang of regret. Not all religious myths were true, as he would soon learn. Myths about Jesus, Tom Cruise, Scientology's Xenu, even the "Eternal Return" - none of these stories held the truth. But this was not something to be mourned; it was a testament to the boundless imagination and creativity of humanity.

Gellius, initially hesitant, ultimately accepted his fate. With newfound understanding that he had some freedom in how he would represent Death, he agreed to take on the role. As I appointed him my successor, I knew that this ordinary bathroom was not just a humble space but the gateway to the universe itself. The vastness of places he would visit as the new representation of Death stretched before me like an endless sea of possibilities.

And so, with a heart full of both nostalgia and anticipation, I bid farewell to my role as the embodiment of Death, leaving behind a world that would forever be entwined with the echoes of our shared history.
